ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, approving the Regulations implementing Law 10/2010; Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio, creating the Oficina Central de Titularidad Real and amending the Mercantile Registry Regulations; Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo, de los Mercados de Valores y de los Servicios de Inversión (beneficial ownership transparency framework); Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital; forward-looking application of Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (EU Single AML/CFT Rulebook) from 10 July 2027.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incorporation of any legal-person shareholder, including its current directors and registered shareholding structure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State or equivalent registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the country-of-origin competent authority, followed by sworn Spanish translation; consular legalization if the jurisdiction is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal Record Certificate (Certificado de Antecedentes Penales) for each natural-person director or manager; FBI Identity History Summary for U.S. resident individuals
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice, FBI, or national criminal-records authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in the country of issuance, followed by sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport bio-data page for each natural-person shareholder and each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the individual's country of residence or the issuing passport authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification plus Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement, or rental contract issued within the last three months) for each shareholder and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, banking institution, or landlord
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy and sworn Spanish translation; apostille required where issuance originates from a public office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming good standing, no-overdraft status, and account conduct of each founding party (required by Spanish banks under internal CDD and recommended for SEPBLAC risk profiling)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-authenticated letter delivered through regulated banking channels; it cannot be apostilled and requires sworn translation when used before a Spanish notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all shareholders, directors and the ultimate beneficial owner against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List maintained by the European External Action Service; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the OFAC SDN List and the OFAC 50% ownership rule, required due to USD-denominated Mercury ACH and wire transfer rails; (iv) SEPBLAC advisories and Banco de España published cautions; and (v) Politically Exposed Person indicators under Law 10/2010 article 14(2), covering family members and known close associates, with PEP status maintained for 24 months after leaving public office. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for PEPs, shell holding structures, non-resident directors, and cross-border performance-based affiliate flows; source-of-wealth documentation and transaction-pattern analytics are required for high-risk counterparties in pay-per-lead, crypto, gambling and anonymous merchant categories, following SEPBLAC and FATF interpretive guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sede Electrónica del Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry electronic portal) accessible via www.rmc.es; the Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social is filed electronically in S3 format through the Registradores de España platform or coordinated through the notary assigned to the incorporation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be composed of words in Spanish or any of Spain's co-official languages (Catalan, Galician, Basque, Valencian); Latin script is mandatory; acronyms and initials are permissible provided they are pronounceable; foreign-language terms are admitted only when adapted to the Spanish alphabet and not merely descriptive of the statutory activity; every name must end with the mandatory type suffix 'Sociedad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.'; the Registro Mercantil Central verifies identity and phonetic similarity against existing Spanish companies and Spanish branches of EEA companies per Real Decreto 1582/2008, articles 3 to 6.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate is valid for 3 months and is not extendable. Upon a motivated rejection (identity or phonetic similarity, prohibited token, or failure to include the S.L. suffix), the applicant may: (i) immediately re-submit an electronic request proposing up to three alternative denominations in priority order on the RMC portal; (ii) file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month of notification of the refusal, attaching the rejected certificate and supporting legal argument; and (iii) if the appeal is dismissed, file a contentious-administrative claim (recurso contencioso-administrativo) before the Audiencia Nacional within two months of the dismissal notification. Re-application adding a distinctive coined or geographic token is the fastest practical remediation path.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is accepted for a digital media arbitrage company provided a real, physical address inside Spanish territory is designated as the domicilio social and can receive service of process, tax notices and registry communications; pure post-office boxes are prohibited. The founding notary requires a demonstrable title of use (lease, sublease, or accommodation agreement) over the registered-office address. Virtual-office and serviced-desk arrangements are common in the ISIC 7310 sector but trigger enhanced customer due diligence at Spanish banks and SEPBLAC; appointment of a Spanish tax and legal representative is strongly recommended. Foreign-managed decisions must be formalized in minutes that identify the Spanish office as the place where management is legally deemed exercised.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Baseline 35% probability of an unannounced SEPBLAC or AEAT physical inspection within the first 24 months for a virtual-office structure. The risk elevates to 55-65% if the entity exhibits anonymous affiliate payment flows, same-day fund sweeps to foreign accounts, frequent UBO or director changes, or inconsistent VAT filings. A physically leased office with staff, local contracts, and demonstrable economic substance reduces the inspection probability to below 15%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RMC electronic tariff of approximately EUR 13.00 inclusive of electronic stamp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff under Real Decreto 1426/1989, standard EUR 450-700 band for a non-complex SL deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First inscription of the company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry (inscripción primera)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), as amended by Ley 18/2022, de 28 de septiembre (Crea y Crece) — Arts. 3, 4, 20-23, 28-31, 40, 62, 102, 133, 210, 283; Ley 14/2013 de Apoyo a los Emprendedores (Art. 15, telematic DUE incorporation); Regulation of the Commercial Registry (RD 1784/1996).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (registration of the deed); Ministry of Justice, Madrid.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (notarial deed of incorporation) followed by legal inscription in the Registro Mercantil Provincial; where the DUE/CIRCE fast-track is used, the electronic Documento Único Electrónico replaces the paper instrument.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital: €1 under Art. 4 LSC as amended by Ley 18/2022 (the former €3,000 floor having been repealed; however, if capital is below €3,000 the company must appropriate 25% of annual net profits to legal reserve until capital plus reserve reach €3,000 and is barred from profit distributions below that threshold). The entire subscription must be fully paid up (desembolso íntegro) before the deed is executed, evidenced by a bank certificate/escrow account opened in the company's formation name; cash contributions are deposited in an account held in the future SL's name and remain blocked until incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], S.L.

(1) The incorporation of the Company is ratified; the subscription and full payment of the entire share capital of €[•] is confirmed on the basis of the bank certificate attached to the deed.

(2) The registered office is adopted at [Address], Madrid, Spain, as the seat of central administration and statutory records.

(3) [Name] is appointed Sole Administrator and accepts the office. The Administrator is expressly empowered to open bank accounts, enter into contracts within the corporate purpose, and represent the Company before the Commercial Registry, the tax authorities, and third parties.

(4) The Administrator shall implement the commercial registration, definitive NIF, book legalization, and any municipal activity declaration required for commencement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Corporate Name (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), Madrid — online SOREC/DICIREG application or postal filing to C/ Velázquez, 36.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit application Form CIRCE/SOREC 005 with three name choices in descending order of priority. The Central Registry verifies no identical or confusingly similar existing denomination and issues the negative name certificate, which is valid for two months (renewable) pending registration.
required_dossiers: Copy of the promoting shareholder's passport/DNI/NIE
Power of attorney if a representative files
Proof of payment of the certification fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the denomination is refused for similarity, re-file with alternative names at no penalty; an improperly denied application may be appealed via recurso de alzada to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Deposit and Bank Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Credit institution licensed by the Banco de España, or the chosen notary for a formal deposit (depósito del capital social).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the future SL ('en formación') and deposit the fully subscribed capital. Obtain a bank certificate (certificado de saldo o titularidad) expressly stating the account holder is the SL in formation, the account number, and the balance; the notary will examine this certificate when executing the deed. If the bank refuses a pre-NIF account, deposit the same amount with the notary, who will record it in the deed.
required_dossiers: Identification of all shareholders and proposed administrator
Draft Modelo 036 for the provisional NIF
Compliance documents of the bank's AML questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires a legal-entity NIF, present the notarial draft and apply for the provisional NIF before deposit (Art. 22 LSC); if the bank nonetheless refuses, proceed with the notarial deposit route.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must apply for a Spanish NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) using Form 036 via an AEAT tax representative. Required supporting documents include a notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation, proof of foreign tax residence, power of attorney (from modelo 036 or 840), and identity documentation of the legal representative. The application is submitted electronically with an APK digital certificate or through a designated proxy; the NIF is issued once the foreign entity is registered in the Registro de Extranjeros and, where relevant, the Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores. The NIF remains valid for tax obligations and must be quoted on all returns, invoices, and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a check-the-box or elective pass-through regime for Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada. An SL is irrebuttably treated as a separate taxable entity resident in Spain when incorporated under Spanish law. No hybrid mismatch elections are available; however, EU ATAD and DAC6 hybrid mismatch rules may reclassify or deny benefits where an arrangement exploits discrepancies between Member States. Certain Spanish tax consolidation elections are available under articles 58–64 of Ley 27/2014 for groups, and specific attributions apply to permanent establishments of non-resident entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general minimum economic threshold triggers VAT registration; any person carrying out taxable business activities in Spain must register. For non-established foreign businesses, the supply of taxable goods or services in Spanish territory obligatorily requires VAT registration from the first transaction. A reduced threshold of EUR 35,000 applies to EU distance sales of goods (B2C) under the special distance-selling scheme, and EUR 10,000 for cross-border intra-EU services, with other EU/third-country distance thresholds governed by the OSS (One-Stop Shop) regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain has implemented the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) for VAT taxpayers exceeding EUR 6 million annual turnover and certain other groups; SII requires near-real-time electronic submission of invoice records to AEAT within 4 business days. The 'Ley Crea y Crece' (Law 18/2022) mandates structured electronic B2B e-invoicing, scheduled under forthcoming implementing regulation, using facturae or comparable XML formats with digital signature. The Verifactu system further institutionalizes tamper-proof invoice integrity and QR/tracking codes. No universal continuous transaction control (CTC) clearance or central digital stamping is required for all invoices, but SII and Verifactu effectively impose real-time fiscal reporting for covered taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Spain to non-EU destinations are subject to 0% VAT when the goods are dispatched or transported out of the EU, provided the exporter retains proof of physical exit. For B2B services, including digital advertising media buying, the place of supply is the customer's establishment location; when the recipient is established outside Spain, the service is generally outside the scope of Spanish VAT and no domestic VAT is chargeable (reverse charge follows in the customer's jurisdiction). Services rendered to non-business customers outside the EU may also be zero-rated or outside scope under Article 69 of the VAT Law, subject to evidence of destination. Eligibility requires the supplier to have completed the SII/ordinary VAT return, reliable documentary proof of exit or customer location, and valid foreign VAT/TIN numbers where applicable. Zero-rating may be refused where the supplier knew or should have known that incoterms, transport documentation, or payment routing did not support a genuine export or offshore supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Documento Único Administrativo) via the AEAT customs system (nota de aduana)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Proof of transport (CMR freight contract, P&I insurance certificate, or container tracking logs)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 confirmation evidencing foreign payment receipt
Foreign customer VAT registration certificate or tax residency certificate for offshore B2B services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT strictly audits export zero-rating claims and VAT refunds; false declarations, missing exit proofs, or staged circular exports trigger retroactive VAT assessment with late surcharges (recargo de apremio), default interest, and penalties of up to 150% of the tax loss. Gross negligence or fraud may incur penalties under Article 170 Ley General Tributaria of EUR 6,000 per declarant for non-filed returns, plus criminal sanctions for tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000. Additionally, the State Agency for Tax Administration may claw back any wrongly zero-rated input VAT reclaimed and may disqualify the exporter from deferred export procedures (autorización de deposito distinto del aduanero or EORI privileges).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) is Spain’s central bank and national competent authority for specified financial-sector and balance-of-payments reporting functions. The European Central Bank and applicable EU institutions also govern monetary policy and relevant payment and prudential rules. Spain’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business administers foreign-investment reporting and screening matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is an EU and euro-area member. The euro is freely convertible, and ordinary current-account and capital-account cross-border transfers are generally permitted without prior exchange-control approval, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, tax rules, investment-screening requirements, and reporting obligations. A Spanish SL may generally receive foreign shareholder funding, pay bona fide overseas suppliers, and remit dividends or other lawful distributions. Dividend remittances require distributable profits, valid corporate approvals, compliance with Spanish withholding-tax rules and applicable treaty or EU relief, and adequate supporting records. Banks may require evidence of the transaction’s commercial purpose, source of funds, beneficial ownership, tax residence, and corporate authorization. Foreign-investment declarations and statistical reporting may apply depending on the investor, transaction, amount, and applicable rules; confirm current thresholds and forms with Spanish counsel and the receiving bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no general mandatory conversion ratio or deadline requiring exporters to convert foreign-currency receipts into euros. Export receipts may generally be retained in foreign currency, subject to ordinary tax, accounting, sanctions, AML, and applicable statistical-reporting requirements. The SL should retain invoices, contracts, payment records, and reconciliation evidence and make any applicable Banco de España or foreign-investment reports.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. An EU-authorized electronic money institution or payment institution may provide permitted payment and safeguarding services, including eligible cross-border transfers, subject to its authorization, passporting status, product terms, and AML controls. An EMI account is not necessarily a bank deposit and may not provide deposit-guarantee protection. Offshore providers without appropriate EU authorization or valid passporting should not be used to conduct regulated payment services in Spain. Fintech onboarding does not replace the need for a Spanish bank relationship where required for incorporation, tax, payroll, lending, or counterparties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that every director attend a bank branch in person to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available where the bank accepts the identity-verification method and documentation. Banks may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, video interview, original or notarized documents, Spanish tax identifiers, or local authorized signatories under their risk policies. Confirm requirements with the selected bank before incorporation and account funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or layered ownership, nominee arrangements, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry extracts and constitutional documents for each ownership layer; certified ownership chart through to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and proof of address; Spanish NIE/NIF documentation where applicable; beneficial-ownership declarations; and board resolutions identifying authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear origin of shareholder capital, unusually large initial transfers, or payments from an unrelated third party or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder funding agreement or subscription documentation; source-of-funds and, where requested, source-of-wealth evidence; originating account statements; tax returns, audited accounts, sale records, or other corroborating evidence; transfer instructions identifying the shareholder and investment purpose; and Spanish corporate approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Affiliate media buying with rapid, high-volume, or circular flows between the SL, advertising platforms, affiliate networks, clients, and related parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan and flow-of-funds diagram; customer, publisher, and platform contracts; invoices and campaign statements; evidence of advertising placement and lead-generation services; pricing and commission methodology; reconciliation from campaign spend to client billing and affiliate receipts; and written related-party arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments inconsistent with the stated business, including unexplained cash, personal-account funding, cryptoasset-related flows, third-party collections, or transactions involving sanctioned or high-risk locations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written payment policy restricting funds to documented business flows; complete bank and ledger reconciliations; counterparty due-diligence records; invoices and delivery evidence; sanctions-screening results; explanation and supporting documents for any exceptional transaction; and evidence that personal and corporate funds are segregated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear tax residence, substance, management location, or mismatch between registered activity and actual cross-border operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish incorporation and tax-registration records; registered-office and operating-address evidence; director and employee details; accounting and tax filings; service and employment contracts; evidence of decision-making and business activity; and a concise explanation of each operating jurisdiction and payment corridor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Fund the SL from an account held in the shareholder’s own name through SEPA credit transfer for euro transfers within the SEPA area or SWIFT for other currencies and corridors. Identify the remitter as the shareholder and describe the transfer accurately as share capital, share premium, shareholder loan, or another legally documented funding category; do not use a misleading payment purpose or a generic third-party remitter. Provide the bank with the subscription or loan documents, corporate approvals, beneficial-ownership information, source-of-funds evidence, and any requested foreign-investment reporting information. A bank may request additional documentation or reject a transfer under its AML, sanctions, or risk policies. Reconcile the receipt to the accounting records and applicable tax and statistical reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Pay documented euro-area counterparties through SEPA credit transfer and use SWIFT for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. Use a bank wire with accurate beneficiary, invoice, contract, and payment-purpose information for routine advertising-platform, affiliate-network, software, and service-provider settlements. Documentary commercial letters of credit are generally available through banks but are usually relevant only where transaction size, goods, and counterparty risk justify them; they are not a standard settlement rail for digital advertising services. SWIFT MT103 is a legacy customer-credit-transfer message; cross-border transfers may be processed under ISO 20022, including pacs.008, depending on the sending and receiving institutions. Retain invoices, campaign or service evidence, approvals, and payment confirmations for accounting, tax, and bank review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards for documented, genuine commercial exposures, subject to bank onboarding, suitability and appropriateness requirements where applicable, and the provider’s documentation requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards where offered by an appropriately authorized counterparty and suitable for the relevant currency and exposure; settlement and product legality depend on the currency, counterparty, and applicable EU rules.
Currency swaps for documented liquidity or funding needs, subject to counterparty approval, contractual terms, collateral requirements, and applicable conduct and reporting rules.
Spot FX conversion for operational receipts and payments; maintain an approved counterparty list, exposure limits, authorization controls, and transaction records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts and Management Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after approval by the General Shareholders' Meeting (typically by 30 June for calendar year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 300,000 EUR and risk of company dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if net turnover exceeds 2 million EUR, total assets exceed 1 million EUR, or average employees exceed 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC) or IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain and update Beneficial Ownership Register; annual accuracy confirmation and filing of changes to Registro Mercantil

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 30-150 USD annually for registered office or agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 400-3,500 USD depending on audit requirement and company size

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly created entities may qualify for a 15% rate for the first tax period with a positive taxable base and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory eligibility conditions and exclusions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying newly created companies may apply the 15% rate described above. Other relevant incentives may include research and development deductions, technological innovation deductions, employment-related incentives, capitalization-reserve deductions, and tax credits under specific statutory conditions. The participation exemption may apply to qualifying dividends and capital gains from substantial shareholdings, generally subject to a minimum 5% participation and a one-year holding requirement, with statutory limitations.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite; Spanish corporate tax losses generally have no statutory expiry period. Their utilization is subject to annual taxable-base limitation rules, including 70% of the pre-loss taxable base for companies with annual turnover below EUR 20 million, 50% for turnover of at least EUR 20 million and below EUR 60 million, and 25% for turnover of at least EUR 60 million, generally with a EUR 1 million minimum offset. Additional group and anti-abuse restrictions may apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax and Non-Resident Income Tax return for permanent establishments; mandatory electronic filing through the Spanish Tax Agency electronic headquarters (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT Sede Electrónica), generally using an electronic certificate or Cl@ve where permitted.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year company, the ordinary filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the last day is not a business day, the applicable electronic filing rule extends the deadline to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered address, legal form, tax period, activity classification, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish entity's NIF and registered details. Foreign shareholders, parent entities, and beneficial owners are reported separately where requested; do not substitute a foreign tax number for the Spanish company's NIF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable corporate tax regime, accounting period, turnover indicators, group membership, tax consolidation status, and special-regime elections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Spanish SL owned by non-residents normally files under the ordinary Spanish corporate tax regime unless it validly elects for a special regime. Non-resident ownership does not remove Spanish filing obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result before tax reconciled to the Spanish corporate tax base through permanent and temporary adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and expenses attributable to the Spanish taxpayer. Cross-border service, advertising, financing, royalty, and management charges must be supported by contracts, evidence of performance, and arm's-length analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for exempt dividends, capital gains, and other income subject to statutory exemption or limitation rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the percentage ownership, holding period, participation conditions, underlying taxation, and anti-abuse requirements for foreign subsidiaries. Do not claim exemption solely because the recipient or payer is located in the European Union.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening tax losses, losses generated in the current period, utilized losses, annual utilization limitation, and closing balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain evidence of the losses and observe Spanish utilization limits. Transactions involving changes of ownership, dormant entities, or acquired loss companies require anti-abuse review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of qualifying related-party transactions and, where applicable, the corresponding information forms and documentation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border transactions with the foreign parent, affiliates, shareholders, directors, and related service providers consistently with the transfer-pricing file and statutory information-return thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments, applicable rate, tax liability before credits, and applicable reductions or deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the ordinary 25% rate unless the company satisfies the legal requirements for the 15% newly created-entity rate or another specific incentive.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research and development, technological innovation, employment, investment, foreign-tax, and other legally available credits or deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign-tax credits only within statutory limits and retain foreign tax certificates, payment evidence, and income allocation calculations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit installment payments under Modelo 202 and Spanish withholding or payment-on-account amounts attributable to the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all Modelo 202 payments and Spanish withholding certificates to the general ledger and bank records. Foreign withholding is not automatically creditable without statutory supporting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Balance payable or refundable and payment details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance, direct-debit instruction, payment reference, refund request, and electronic filing confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the Spanish bank account or approved payment mechanism is valid and preserve the electronic filing receipt, payment NRC, and complete submitted return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payments on account generally filed in April, October, and December.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the applicable calculation method and turnover rules. Large companies may be subject to the minimum installment-payment regime and a different electronic payment timetable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax payable may trigger a fixed penalty under the General Tax Law, generally EUR 200, reduced by 50% for voluntary filing without prior notice where applicable. Late filing with tax payable generally triggers a surcharge of 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months, with a 15% surcharge after 12 months plus late-payment interest; the surcharge may be reduced by 25% if statutory payment conditions are satisfied. Incorrect returns may trigger separate penalties of 50% of unpaid tax for ordinary tax-base concealment, increasing to 100% or 150% for qualified or fraudulent conduct. Failure to make installment payments may generate interest, surcharges, and penalty assessments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply through Spanish implementation where the parent satisfies, among other conditions, the minimum participation, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, and anti-abuse requirements. The domestic exemption is not automatic and requires documentary support.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain a valid tax-residence certificate from the recipient's tax authority, verify treaty eligibility and beneficial-ownership or anti-abuse requirements, classify the payment correctly, and apply the treaty rate at source only where Spanish administrative requirements are satisfied. If relief is not applied at source, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue the refund procedure through the AEAT using the relevant non-resident withholding documentation. Retain the certificate, ownership-chain evidence, payment records, treaty analysis, and beneficial-owner representation. Certificates should be current under Spanish administrative practice and renewed when required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Under domestic non-resident tax rules, the general rate is commonly 24% for royalties and interest paid to non-residents outside the EU/EEA, while a 19% rate generally applies to qualifying EU/EEA recipients. Interest and certain royalty payments may be exempt under Spanish implementation of the EU Interest and Royalties Directive if the corporate, ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions are met. Applicable treaty rates vary by treaty and commonly reduce source taxation on interest and royalties, frequently to approximately 5% to 10%, but the specific treaty must be checked before payment. Spanish VAT, deductibility, beneficial-ownership, and withholding obligations must be analyzed separately.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 aggregate annual related-party transaction threshold with the same related person or entity and under the same type of transaction generally determines whether the Spanish local documentation exemption may apply, subject to exclusions and transaction-specific rules. A Spanish master file is generally required where the multinational group has consolidated turnover of at least EUR 45 million, subject to statutory exceptions. Documentation may still be required below the threshold where the tax authority requests it or where specific transactions and anti-abuse rules apply.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a single standalone economic-substance regulation equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Nevertheless, Spanish anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership principles, the principal-purpose test where applicable, controlled-foreign-company rules, interest limitation rules, and EU anti-tax-avoidance measures require genuine commercial rationale, personnel and decision-making capacity appropriate to the functions performed, real control over risks, and documentary evidence. A Spanish SL performing digital advertising media buying and affiliate lead generation should maintain local operational substance proportionate to its claimed functions, including personnel or outsourced-function oversight, decision records, bank-account control, contracts, campaign evidence, customer and supplier records, and transfer-pricing support.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent tax assessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of advertising revenue, fictitious expenses, false invoices, undeclared affiliate commissions, manipulated campaign costs, or fraudulent transfer-pricing adjustments causing tax loss exceeding the criminal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax fraud generally becomes a criminal offense where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax and period, punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the defrauded amount, together with loss of public subsidies and tax benefits for three to six years. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or use of organizations or intermediaries, may attract imprisonment of two to six years and higher ancillary consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability where they participate in, authorize, or knowingly facilitate the conduct. Courts may order asset seizure, civil restitution, disqualification, and precautionary measures. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be imposed judicially. Corporate veil piercing is exceptional and requires abuse of legal personality, fraud, or asset-shielding conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing and undocumented affiliate media expenditure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording fabricated supplier invoices, recycling invoices between related entities, charging media spend without proof of delivery, or deducting costs unrelated to the Spanish business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments may deny deductions, assess unpaid corporate tax and interest, and impose penalties commonly ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax depending on concealment and fraud. Serious invoicing offenses may attract penalties based on the invoice amount or tax amount under the General Tax Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face joint or subsidiary tax liability where they fail to exercise required management diligence or deliberately cause non-compliance. Knowing participation in fabricated documentation may also create criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Shifting Spanish advertising margins to a foreign affiliate through unsupported service fees, royalties, data charges, financing costs, or commissions; failure to price related-party transactions at arm's length; or maintaining inconsistent local files and financial accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may adjust the taxable base to arm's-length value, assess tax, late-payment interest, and transfer-pricing penalties. Failure to maintain or provide required documentation may generate fixed or percentage-based penalties, including penalties linked to the omitted or incorrectly documented transaction amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil or tax liability for deliberate profit diversion, falsified records, or obstruction. Cross-border group approval does not eliminate local director duties or the Spanish company's independent arm's-length obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees to an intermediary without withholding, applying treaty relief without a valid tax-residence certificate, routing payments through conduit entities, or claiming EU exemptions without satisfying ownership, subject-to-tax, holding-period, or anti-abuse conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer may be assessed for unwithheld tax, late-payment interest, and withholding penalties. Treaty or directive relief may be denied, and anti-abuse rules may recharacterize the payment or recipient. Penalties depend on the unpaid amount and degree of culpability and may be materially increased for concealment or fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be pursued for subsidiary tax liability where they knowingly authorize defective withholding or fail to implement reasonable controls. Criminal tax exposure may arise if the resulting tax fraud exceeds the applicable criminal threshold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Value-added tax carousel, invoice-chain, or advertising-service fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using missing-trader suppliers, fabricated EU service transactions, false reverse-charge entries, improper input-VAT deductions, or circular payments disguised as media purchases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT may be reassessed with interest and penalties generally calculated by reference to the unpaid or improperly claimed amount. Serious or very serious conduct may trigger penalties of 50%, 100%, or 150% of the tax impact. Organized VAT fraud may constitute a criminal offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may incur criminal, civil, and tax liability when they knowingly use fraudulent suppliers or control the transaction chain. Asset freezing and judicial precautionary measures may be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party funds, disguising beneficial ownership, using personal or unrelated bank accounts, structuring payments, failing to identify customers or beneficial owners, or ignoring suspicious affiliate payment flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious breaches may result in public or private reprimands, monetary penalties that can reach millions of euros or statutory percentages of net worth, and temporary or permanent restrictions on holding management positions. Criminal money-laundering offenses may carry imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and compliance officers may be personally sanctioned where they caused, tolerated, or failed to prevent the breach. Courts may order asset seizure and travel restrictions where justified; imprisonment is possible for criminal laundering or terrorist-financing conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining double books, destroying campaign records, falsifying board approvals, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, backdating intercompany agreements, or misrepresenting the company's actual functions and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include tax assessments, accounting and corporate-law penalties, denial of deductions, administrative fines, director disqualification, and criminal liability for accounting or document offenses where statutory elements are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for creditor or tax damage caused by breach of fiduciary duties, unlawful distributions, insolvency-related misconduct, or deliberate record falsification. Piercing the corporate veil remains exceptional and fact-dependent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper dividend distribution and insolvency-related repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without distributable reserves, repatriating funds while insolvent, disguising shareholder withdrawals as service fees, or making related-party payments that prejudice creditors or the Spanish tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlawful distributions may require repayment with interest and may produce director liability, creditor claims, tax reassessment, and insolvency sanctions. Fraudulent asset transfers or creditor prejudice may result in civil or criminal proceedings and disqualification from managing companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore assets, compensate the company or creditors, cover insolvency shortfalls in qualifying cases, and face disqualification. Judicial travel restrictions or imprisonment are possible only where ordered under applicable civil or criminal proceedings.
